Provisional name of the skull-shaped island where Ladder waits.

Provisional pirate name in the disguised-brother trap.
Provisional pirate name. Her Kurumi disguise and both rescue-choice outcomes are retained.
Provisional name of Ladder's sister; her haughty speech and post-defeat crying are retained. Native label 2893 uses this spelling; saved nicknames are separate.
Provisional place name in the false Kurumi's introduction, not changed to Water Blue.

Provisional Gold Blue island name in Ladder's warning.
Provisional Gold Blue elder name; Fu is his elder twin. Native speaker labels remain Japanese.
Provisional name of Ho's elder twin; conducts the Pao Tai training trial.

Provisional Gold Blue boss name; abbreviated Linlin when the source uses リンリン. Native label 2900 uses this spelling; saved nicknames are separate.
Short name of Li Linlin, the expelled Gold Blue pupil and leader of its invading army.
Provisional hopping-vampire character name; stutter and hohi laughter retained.
Martial-arts balance of mind, skill and body. Compact dialogue uses mind/skill/body, with initial capitalization as needed.
Golden fragment associated with Gold Blue. Crowded dialogue and the nine-cell inventory label use Gold. Distinct from the legendary Caramel.

terms.source: デスペラーマウンテン
terms.note: Provisional mountain name. Crowded dialogue uses Mt. Despera.

terms.source: ロボポンへの　みち／もえよ　ロボポン／ロボポン　ききいっぱつ
terms.english: Way of Robopon / Enter Robopon / The Big Robopon
terms.note: Regional hint 1913 parodies the Japanese titles of The Way of the Dragon, Enter the Dragon and The Big Boss. English uses compact Robopon film-title puns. Keeps the water and one-inch-punch references.
The sixth fragment; crowded dialogue, the acquisition message and the eight-cell inventory label use Earth. Record 2141 says it alone grants entry to Despera Mountain, without the other five.

Provisional name of the whale-shaped Robopon and the ship used for deep-area travel. Doluppi in record 2130 is an intentional false identification, immediately corrected. Native label 2839 uses this spelling; saved nicknames are separate.
Provisional name for the rising islands, retaining the floating wordplay; hint 2302 spells the suffix とう instead of じま. Conditions include ship proximity, moving away and defeating a battler.

Provisional rendering of the literal name in main warning 2145. Alternate warning 2346 uses the entered-name command instead; both source forms are retained. Native label 2857 uses this spelling; saved nicknames are separate.

terms.source: ゴー フォー ブロック
terms.note: The impostors say block rather than the expected Go for broke. Retained as a source malapropism. Record 2059 also retains Gold Blue where 2054 says Land Blue.
Seventh fragment, named by Linlin in 2389. Main finale 2477 awards it; the acquisition message and inventory label 3679 use Sun. Linlin does not award it in the rematch scene.

terms.source: カニオ／サバゾー／ウニコ／サザエ／ワカメ
terms.note: Don Oyaji's baby-name skit in 2376. Retains Japanese sea-food names and puns: crab, mackerel, sea urchin, turban shell and seaweed. The dialogue is deliberately silly.
Musketeers 2425: no miraculous favorable wind or luck against the player and Caramela; no aircraft-attack reference.
Musketeers farewell 2430; preserved as a farewell to the sea/world. No additional region is inferred.

Provisional antagonist name. Uses a mechanical body and seeks a Zero empire. Dialogue describes restored human feeling, then his decision to die as a human; no new backstory or resurrection is inferred.
Top Robopon battler rank claimed by Dr. Zero in 2453; provisional compact rendering.

terms.source: カラメルの話し方：オラ／モシ
terms.note: Revival monologue 2481 uses stutters, ya and informal phrasing. Its repeated eye-reading requests, pauses, joke and departure remain; no real-world regional dialect is asserted.

terms.source: あしたからさきのみらい
terms.note: Zero's dying explanation in 2488 of what Caramel sees in the player's eyes and will grant. The hero never states a spoken wish; this ambiguity is retained.

terms.source: われわれはしばらくやすむことにするよ
terms.note: Alternate Musketeers farewell 2574 says rest, unlike main 2428's leaving the sea. Their different source meanings are retained.

terms.source: ラム・マイティ・ミカチ
terms.note: Alternate threat 2637 names this crew, replacing main 2490 Punch/Dandy/Mikachi. The full cast uses the same explicit page before Mikachi at source-control index 36; all original colors remain.

terms.source: ２６３６：あしたをとりもどしたのです
terms.note: Closing narration credits the player's courage, strength and moral resolve for restoring tomorrow and lasting peace. The condensed English says brave, strong and just; its source location alone does not establish which route calls it.
